summary.text: A 36-year-old gravida 6 para 3 woman at 6 weeks 4 days of gestational age presented in July 2020 with worsening dyspnea and chest pain and was found to have COVID-19, with asthma, chronic hypertension and morbid obesity class III in her history. Three days earlier she had visited a different hospital for vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain and been discharged with a pregnancy of unknown location.

She received low-flow nasal cannula oxygen and was admitted for supportive therapy; chest X-ray raised concern for atypical or viral pneumonia and she had severe orthopnoea and initial lymphopenia. Serum B-hCG was 3,838 mIU/mL, and transvaginal ultrasound showed no intrauterine pregnancy and a right adnexal mass highly suggestive of a right tubal ectopic pregnancy with no free fluid.

A multidisciplinary team weighed her comorbidities; expectant management was judged not possible and she was deemed a high-risk surgical candidate. A two-dose intramuscular methotrexate protocol was given, with an hCG drop above 15% and mild transaminitis afterward. She improved clinically, was stable for discharge by hospital day 10, and had outpatient hCG follow-up until non-pregnant levels were reached.
